thread.title: Fitbit: Shares Pop as Its Ace Kids’ Tracker Hits Stores

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Fitbit: Shares Pop as Its Ace Kids’ Tracker Hits Stores
text:
Photo: Fitbit By David Marino-Nachison June 11, 2018 12:29 p.m. ET Investors cheered Fitbit ’s (FIT) Monday news that its Ace kids’ fitness tracker was available globally, with the company’s shares rising 10% by early afternoon on the announcement.
The Barron’s Next 50 company announced the device—along with its Versa smartwatch, which it recently said passed its millionth shipment—in March, saying it would land in the second quarter. On a May conference call with investors, CEO James Park said it was “a little early to say if the product’s really going to be on the shelf in Q2.” In that context, the launch is perhaps a pleasant surprise.
Newsletter Sign-up And there was another surprise on Monday: A tweet , and post , from noted short-seller Andrew Left, whose Citron Research called the company “one of the most underappreciated med-tech stories in the market.”
Fitbit is generally turning toward watches from fitness trackers along with the rest of the wearables business. The company hopes the Ace will appeal to parents, and its price point comes in a bit lighter than most of its other wristbands.
It’s also a health-focused device, with Fitbit seeking to make itself the brand of choice in that segment even as Apple (AAPL) and others seek to gobble up share . (The company’s health efforts are the main thrust of Citron’s report, which targeted a $15 share price that’s more than twice current levels.)
If Ace succeeds, it might give some life to the category while offering shoppers another opportunity to get the company’s products in the home.
More About Barron’s Next Learn more about Barron’s Next The Barron’s Next 50 ”We feel pretty good about Fitbit Ace,” Park said on the May call, a transcript of which is on SeekingAlpha . “And…there’s a role for innovation to play in reinvigorating the trackers, and we’re going to continue to innovate in trackers but do it in a more cost-efficient way.”
Some analysts are starting to see opportunity in Fitbit’s shares , which remain well-below their post-IPO 2015 highs. Lately, meanwhile, investors have agreed: The stock is up substantially since 2018 lows hit in early April, and recently crossed into positive territory for the year, the latest climb coming after Q1 operating results included projections of a break-even 2018.
This story has been updated to note the Citron report.
